ai.description: Oligodon affinis is a small snake reaching 35 cm. It is brown with a dark-edged vertebral stripe and a distinct chevron-shaped mark on the nape. The belly is yellowish with dark lateral spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Oligodon affinis* is best distinguished by its plain, unpatterned reddish-brown back, which lacks the distinct dark crossbars or blotches seen in other Kukri snakes.
ai.habitat: *Oligodon affinis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in leaf litter and under logs within the Western Ghats at elevations up to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Western Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon affinis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs deposited in concealed terrestrial sites.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon affinis* is found in the Western Ghats of India, primarily across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka, at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,500 meters.
